owasp_top10.name: Broken Access Control
owasp_top10.description: Access control enforces policy such that users cannot act outside of their intended permissions. Failures typically lead to unauthorized information disclosure, modification, or destruction of all data, or performing a business function outside the user's limits.
owasp_top10.impact: Attackers can exploit broken access controls to access unauthorized functionality or data, modify or delete data, perform privileged actions, and gain full admin access.
owasp_top10.fix: Deny by default. Implement server-side access control. Log access control failures. Rate limit API and controller access. Invalidate JWT tokens on logout.

owasp_top10.name: Cryptographic Failures
owasp_top10.description: Failures related to cryptography which often lead to sensitive data exposure or system compromise. Previously known as 'Sensitive Data Exposure'.
owasp_top10.impact: Sensitive data transmitted or stored in cleartext. Weak or outdated cryptographic algorithms. Improper certificate validation.
owasp_top10.fix: Classify sensitive data. Encrypt data at rest and in transit. Use strong, modern cryptography (AES-256, TLS 1.2+). Enforce HTTPS via HSTS. Do not use MD5/SHA1 for passwords.

owasp_top10.name: Injection
owasp_top10.description: Injection flaws occur when untrusted data is sent to an interpreter as part of a command or query. SQL, NoSQL, OS command, LDAP injection are common forms.
owasp_top10.impact: Full database compromise. Authentication bypass. Data exfiltration. Remote code execution. Complete system takeover.
owasp_top10.fix: Use parameterized queries/prepared statements. Validate and sanitize all inputs. Use an ORM. Apply least privilege to database accounts. Use WAF as additional layer.

owasp_top10.name: Insecure Design
owasp_top10.description: Insecure design is a broad category representing different weaknesses, expressed as 'missing or ineffective control design.' This is distinct from insecure implementation.
owasp_top10.impact: Business logic flaws. Missing security controls. Insecure architecture decisions that cannot be fixed by correct implementation.
owasp_top10.fix: Use threat modeling during design. Integrate security requirements in the design phase. Use design patterns with security in mind. Perform security-focused peer reviews.

owasp_top10.name: Security Misconfiguration
owasp_top10.description: Security misconfiguration is the most commonly seen issue. This is commonly a result of insecure default configurations, incomplete or ad hoc configurations, open cloud storage, misconfigured HTTP headers, and verbose error messages.
owasp_top10.impact: Full system compromise. Data leakage. Unauthorized access. Remote code execution via exposed admin panels.
owasp_top10.fix: Implement secure configuration management. Disable unnecessary features. Review and update configurations. Automate configuration validation. Remove default accounts.

owasp_top10.name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
owasp_top10.description: Components such as libraries, frameworks, and other software modules run with the same privileges as the application. If a vulnerable component is exploited, such an attack can facilitate serious data loss or server takeover.
owasp_top10.impact: Remote code execution. Data exfiltration. Denial of service. Full application compromise via known public CVEs.
owasp_top10.fix: Continuously inventory component versions. Monitor for vulnerabilities (CVE databases). Subscribe to security advisories. Apply patches promptly. Remove unused dependencies.

owasp_top10.name: Identification and Authentication Failures
owasp_top10.description: Previously known as 'Broken Authentication'. Confirmation of the user's identity, authentication, and session management is critical.
owasp_top10.impact: Account takeover. Identity fraud. Unauthorized access to sensitive data and functions.
owasp_top10.fix: Implement MFA. Use strong password policies. Limit failed login attempts. Expire sessions properly. Use secure, random session tokens. Do not expose session IDs in URLs.

owasp_top10.name: Software and Data Integrity Failures
owasp_top10.description: This category focuses on making assumptions related to software updates, critical data, and CI/CD pipelines without verifying integrity.
owasp_top10.impact: Malicious code execution via supply chain attacks. Data tampering. Unauthorized system modifications.
owasp_top10.fix: Use digital signatures for software and data. Verify integrity of packages before use. Use trusted update channels. Implement CI/CD security checks. Avoid deserializing untrusted data.

owasp_top10.name: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
owasp_top10.description: Without logging and monitoring, breaches cannot be detected. Insufficient logging and monitoring, including insufficient response, allows attackers to further attack systems.
owasp_top10.impact: Breach goes undetected for extended periods. Loss of forensic evidence. Inability to respond to active attacks. Compliance violations.
owasp_top10.fix: Log all authentication events, access control failures, and input validation failures. Ensure logs have sufficient context. Implement alerting for suspicious activity. Protect logs from tampering.

owasp_top10.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
owasp_top10.description: SSRF flaws occur whenever a web application is fetching a remote resource without validating the user-supplied URL. An attacker can coerce the application to send a crafted request to an unexpected destination.
owasp_top10.impact: Internal network scanning. Accessing cloud metadata services (AWS/GCP IMDS). Remote code execution. Data exfiltration from internal services.
owasp_top10.fix: Validate and sanitize all client-supplied input URLs. Use an allowlist of permitted domains. Disable HTTP redirections. Do not send raw responses to clients. Block private IP ranges in URL validator.
